result:
My verdict on DG5 round 1 (candidate `sha256:8e7d23a3…f8f67b`) is **PASS**, with two findings that I don't consider blocking: one Medium and one Low, neither a mandatory violation.

**Candidate check.** HEAD is `89d30a4`, not the source commit `601d7d2`. The two commits in between change only `docs/delivery/`, which the candidate ID leaves out. Recomputing the ID gives the assigned value with 2172 files, both on the repository and on my disposable clone. The historical validators for DG4, DG3, DG2 and DG1 and `--register DG5` all exit 0.

**What I ran** (in a disposable clone, in English and Arabic):
- **Source text:** all 165 playbook blocks come back through the real API word for word and in order, each with an Arabic translation. B0004, B0016, B0124, B0134, B0136–B0141, B0145, B0147, B0150 and B0152 match the source exactly.
- **No official claims:** every mention of official PMI status or certification in the UI text and exports is a denial. `#0078FF` and the text wordmark are labelled provisional, and the navigation uses the contrast-checked shade `#0071F1`.
- **Acceptance tests:** the ten root acceptance specs passed 30/30 on a production-initialized stack, and the four demo specs passed 12/12 on a demo stack. That includes all twelve walkthrough steps done by the demo users.
- **Integration tests:** 27 files, 340/340 passed. They cover A02, A06, A07, A13, A15, A16 and A22, plus the Studio, procedures, automation, reporting and demo suites.
- **Demo isolation:** a production database holds no demo records or demo users, and `seed-demo` is refused with exit 3.
- **Operating logic:** gate approvals and Finance attestations can't be set as automation actions. Rules A and B are narrow and clearly defined. RAG still comes from the KPI trajectory. The NPV results (−21.04 and −19.12) match a calculation I did independently.

I accepted every decision and disclosure the assignment asked me to judge, with a reason for each in the record. That covers D-163 (a), D-164 (a)–(k), the D-165 observations, Rules A and B, the D-167 clarification, the D-168 roaming wording point, the three ARCH-R3 documentation leftovers and the four unit-test warnings. I traced warning (3), the missing `key`, to a test that doesn't stub the North Star request; it has no product effect.

**Findings:**
- **F-DG5-120 (Medium, REQ-S18-002, owner backend-workflow-engineer).** The seeded roaming demo transformation is end-to-end and sits in the Transform phase, but all six gates G1–G6 are still drafts that were never submitted or approved. Its screens also show Finance-validated benefit value. The product only lets an approved gate move a transformation to the next phase, and it refuses G5 until G4 is approved, so the demo shows a state the product could never produce. The acceptance text ("a gate instance each") passes literally; the problem is that the demo is not coherent (M0348; the playbook's B0009 and B0023).
- **F-DG5-121 (Low, owner frontend-ux-engineer).** The `p2-journeys` "Define → G2" journey ran past its 30 s limit in all three of my runs, in English and Arabic, at load 6–17 while the other two reviews were running. It takes 25–28 s on an idle machine, per the orchestrator's D-169 logs. In serial mode the timeout also skips the auditor (AUD) journey that D-169 talks about. With a 60 s limit all 24 journeys pass (G2 took 37 s, AUD 24–27 s), so the product works; the test just has too little headroom.

**Other notes:**
- **Low disk space.** Only about 1–3 GB was free, shared by three reviewers. I used a shared, sparse clone that leaves out the evidence, run and handback folders, which the candidate ID excludes anyway.
- **My own mistakes.** Three runs failed because of errors in my own probe scripts, not the product. I kept those logs and named them.
- **Not re-run by me.** The three entity-group integration files for S16-012, S16-015 and S16-021. I relied on the implementer suites the register notes name.

The record and findings both pass their gate schemas, and every evidence path exists. My clone and scratch files have been removed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/`:
- `reviews/DG5/round-1/domain-reviewer.json`
- `reviews/DG5/round-1/domain-reviewer.findings.json`
- `test-evidence/DG5/domain/round-1/` (logs, API dumps, EN/AR screenshots, probe scripts)
